subject.title: [Feature]: Add user-visible and confirmable context compaction mechanisms

question: Should OpenClaw add a user-confirmable compaction contract, and what scope is allowed: notify-only, preview/edit/approval, checkpoint rollback, or plugin/provider hooks?
rationale: The request changes public config/defaults, channel-visible UX, raw transcript retention, checkpoint semantics, plugin hooks, and native-runtime boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Adopt a narrow transparency contract
options.body: Keep automatic compaction as the default, add redacted user/operator visibility and checkpoint review first, and defer blocking approvals until retention and authorization semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full approval and editing modes
options.body: Add preview, approve, reject, edit, rollback, and re-expansion modes with explicit redaction, retention, timeout, and upgrade rules.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Document notifyUser, notifier hooks, provider hooks, and checkpoint branch/restore as the supported compaction controls and close future broad requests to narrower bugs.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow transparency contract
recommendation.body: Keep automatic compaction as the default, add redacted user/operator visibility and checkpoint review first, and defer blocking approvals until retention and authorization semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner for the cross-runtime Codex/app-server boundary and broader product-security decision, while checkpoint and notifier details can route to the adjacent owners.
